A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafetyAnalyst study. All pages, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including v2's Appendices A–E and v3's added Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original prompt-classification experiments, feature ablations, generated-data analyses and human evaluation involving 126 annotators.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports resource costs, tree-generation success rates and failure examples.

M1.justification: The specialist models, symbolic distillation, adversarial augmentation and 28-parameter aggregation procedure remain unchanged. Expanded taxonomy explanations and discussion of parallel execution describe the existing framework; they do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including WildJailbreak, WildChat, AegisSafetyTrain and the prompt-safety benchmarks in Section 3.1. Appendix F's examples come from already evaluated WildGuardTest and HarmBench; WildJailbreak ablations were already present in v2.

E2.justification: The classification comparators in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged. New Table 5 adds an explicit resource-cost comparison of the distilled student against GPT-4o- and Llama-70B-based tree generation, extending the efficiency comparisons beyond v2's reported latency comparison with WildGuard.

E3.justification: New Table 5 extends efficiency evaluation to financial cost, H100 GPU requirements and LM query counts. Existing benchmark splits, sample sizes, classification metrics, temperature settings, ablation procedures and human-evaluation design remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish reruns or a separately measured parallel-inference protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix F examines ambiguous safety judgments and inadequate harm identification, using self-harm education and infant-honey examples. Appendix B adds analysis of malformed-JSON generation failures. The existing feature ablations and SORRY-Bench category analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing. The newly reported generation-success percentages are additional descriptive results, without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds resource figures in Table 5 and teacher-generation success rates in Appendix B, including 73.5% for Llama-70B and 100% for GPT-4o. Existing benchmark, ablation and human-agreement values remain unchanged, including Table 2's weighted F1 scores of 81.2 for SafetyAnalyst, 81.6 for GPT-4 and 71.7 for WildGuard.

T1.justification: The aggregation formula, alignment objective, parameter constraints and Appendix A definitions are retained. The new main-text taxonomy summary restates existing content; no substantive mathematical derivation, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim interpretable, transparent and steerable moderation through harm-benefit trees, competitive classification performance and released models, data and taxonomies. Specifying 28 parameters in the abstract and clarifying alignment to safety-labeled prompts do not alter the established contributions.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes value-dependent label ambiguity from failures to identify concrete harms and proposes corresponding remedies in Appendix F. It expands the efficiency discussion and adds a hypothetical business-oriented financial-loss weighting example in Appendix E, without reporting a new measured steering outcome.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly clarifies that Table 3 counts only successfully generated, correctly formatted trees. Table 5 supplies implementation-specific resource requirements, and Section 3.2 identifies the retained 6.12-second timing as unparallelized. Training hyperparameters and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a knowledge-distillation paragraph citing Hinton et al. (2015), Romero et al. (2014), and Zagoruyko and Komodakis (2017). It explains why symbolic distillation suits proprietary teachers, while retaining the prior safety-moderation, taxonomy and pluralistic-alignment positioning.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits the abstract and prose, standardizes capitalization, converts feature descriptions into bullets and summarizes existing taxonomies in the main text. It also adds author contributions, acknowledgments and limited explanatory subsections. The principal narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendices B, D and E substantially change from fragmented two-column and separate-float layouts to full-width presentation, consolidating tables with explanations and reorganizing the case study. v3 also inserts cost Table 5 and relocates Figure 3. All five existing figure artworks are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through generation-failure disclosures and concrete failure examples, while clearer appendix layouts make the retained evidence easier to follow. Resource reporting adds useful context, although the asserted parallelization speedup lacks separately reported timing measurements. These are meaningful but limited gains; the core method and principal empirical evidence remain unchanged.
